questions.stem: The primary purpose of fixation is to:

choices.text: Prevent autolysis and preserve tissue relationships

questions.explanation: Fixation arrests autolysis and microbial degradation while stabilizing tissue components for later processing and staining.

questions.stem: A 12-mm-thick bowel segment arrives in formalin. The best immediate action is to:

choices.text: Trim it to an appropriate thickness and return it to fixative

questions.explanation: Reducing tissue thickness improves fixative penetration and limits an underfixed center.

questions.stem: Tissue edges are firm but the center is soft and poorly preserved. The most likely cause is:
questions.explanation: An edge-to-center preservation gradient is classic for tissue that was too thick or fixed too late.

questions.stem: Routine 10% neutral buffered formalin contains approximately:
questions.explanation: Commercial formalin stock is about 37–40% formaldehyde; a 10% dilution yields about 4% formaldehyde.

questions.stem: For a bone specimen intended for RNA ISH, the preferred decalcification approach is usually:

choices.text: Hydrochloric acid overnight for every specimen

questions.explanation: EDTA is slower but generally preserves morphology, antigens, DNA, and RNA better than strong mineral acids.

questions.stem: Brown-black granular pigment in blood-rich formalin-fixed tissue most strongly suggests:
questions.explanation: Acid formalin hematin forms when formalin becomes acidic, especially in blood-rich tissue.

questions.stem: A laboratory changes formalin vendor for a predictive IHC assay. The best quality action is to:
questions.explanation: Changes in preanalytic reagents that may affect assay performance should be assessed through controlled bridging or validation.

questions.stem: A commonly taught minimum fixative-to-tissue volume is approximately:
questions.explanation: A generous fixative volume, commonly around 10:1, reduces depletion and dilution by tissue fluid.

questions.stem: Variable IHC intensity occurs across specimens with inconsistent fixation times. The best corrective strategy is to:

choices.text: Use the highest antibody concentration on all slides
Ignore fixation because retrieval reverses it completely

questions.explanation: Retrieval cannot reliably reverse all fixation effects; controlled fixation and validated assay conditions are required.

questions.stem: Glutaraldehyde is selected mainly when the priority is:
questions.explanation: Glutaraldehyde strongly crosslinks proteins and provides excellent ultrastructural preservation for electron microscopy.
